note: Grand Central: commuters, redcaps and the information-booth clerk (context). Adults only.

lines.text: Five-twelve to Stamford! Excuse me! Excuse me!
They moved the track again. They move it to keep us humble.
Two hours a day on that train. I've read Tolstoy twice.
Meet me under the clock. Everybody says that. The clock's sick of us.
If I miss this one it's the six-forty and my wife files papers.
Fare's up again. Next year I'm buying a horse.
Bags, mister? Track's a long walk with two suitcases.
Redcap! Carry it to the car, keep your hands for your hat.
Forty years on these floors. I know every crack by its first name.
Mind the cart! Mind the cart, lady, it don't brake.
Track twenty-nine, five fifty-two, all stops. Next.
The shuttle's downstairs, sir. Follow the people who look late.
No, the clock doesn't tell the future. It tells the time. Next.
Lost and found is on the lower level. Bring patience. Next.
Look up. Look at that ceiling. Somebody painted the sky backwards.
Biggest room in the city and still no place to sit.
That photo up there's bigger than my apartment. Nicer, too.
